title: Naturality of the integral comparison on arbitrary permitted-pair arrows.
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Write $F=Lg^*$, $T$ and $H$ for the integral constructible pullback, tensor and internal Hom on its permitted Hom pairs [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations], $\mu_{L,M}:F(T(L,M))\cong T(FL,FM)$ for the canonical integral pullback-tensor comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-construction], and $c_P:F H(P)\to H(FP)$ for the evaluation-defined comparison between the completed integral partial closed data on $Y$ and $X$, $c_P=\operatorname{tr}_X(\mu^{-1}\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_P))$ [def-sf-adic-closed-reindexing-maps, def-pod-partial-closed-interfaces]; a permitted pair $P=(M,N)$ pulls back to a permitted pair $FP$ [lem-pod-reindexing-hom-coefficient-descent]. Then for every arrow $(a,b):P\to Q$ of permitted pairs on $Y$, $c_Q\circ F(H(a,b))=H(F(a,b))\circ c_P$.

lean.statement:
theorem podIntegralHomComparison_naturality :
    ∀ (P Q : (constructibleIntegralHomPairs l E Y).FullSubcategory) (f : P ⟶ Q),
      (constructibleIntegralPullback l E g).map
          ((constructibleIntegralHom l E Y).map f) ≫
        podPartialHomComparison (podIntegralClosed l E Y) (podIntegralClosed l E X)
      (constructibleIntegralPullback l E g) (podIntegralPairs_pullback l E g)
        (canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor l E g) Q =
      podPartialHomComparison (podIntegralClosed l E Y) (podIntegralClosed l E X)
      (constructibleIntegralPullback l E g) (podIntegralPairs_pullback l E g)
        (canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor l E g) P ≫
        (constructibleIntegralHom l E X).map
          ((podPairPullback (constructibleIntegralPullback l E g)
            (constructibleIntegralHomPairs l E Y) (constructibleIntegralHomPairs l E X)
            (podIntegralPairs_pullback l E g)).map f)

proof.text: Prove ambient evaluation dinaturality from the first-variable evaluation law and naturality of the tensor-Hom adjunction counit. Express inverse transposition as tensoring with the morphism followed by evaluation, obtaining its naturality in all three variables. Use the prescribed normalization of the integral transpose and naturality of the completed-tensor unit (the composite of the completion adjunction unit and tensor comparison) to transport this equality to the constructible integral closed data. Specializing the parameter morphism to an identity gives integral evaluation dinaturality.

Apply injectivity of inverse transposition to the desired comparison naturality equation. Parameter naturality and the preceding pair naturality compute its two inverse transposes. Naturality of the inverse pullback-tensor isomorphism moves both the internal-Hom arrow and the contravariant pair arrow past the tensor comparison. Substitute evaluation dinaturality, use functoriality of pullback, and reassociate; the inverse transposes agree. The comparison is the transpose of pulled-back evaluation by definition.
